blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools. The team wants the folder `secrets/` closed to every built-in tool. Which single entry in the settings file does it?

options.says: Ruled out because "`Edit(path)` rules govern all built-in tools that write files", which leaves reading and searching open.

Ruled out because "A rule is written under the name of its family" and the example prints "Grep as Read", so the entry that applies is a `Read` rule, and one for Grep alone leaves Read and the writing tools open.
Ruled out because a scoped Bash rule matches calls "as written", and other spellings "fall through to the permission mode", so it stops neither the search tools nor a different spelling.
A read denial stops reading and searching, and writes at the same path.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools. The agent lists TypeScript sources in a very large repository with `**/*.ts` and receives a result carrying a truncation flag. What should it do next?

options.text: Narrow the search to the folder that the question concerns
options.says: A capped result is a window, and a narrower request brings the rest into view.

options.text: Repeat the same request until the results change
options.says: Ruled out because "Results are sorted by modification time and capped at 100 files", so the same request returns the same window.

options.text: Take the returned files as the complete set and proceed
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude sees a truncation flag in the result and can narrow the pattern", which says the set is incomplete.

options.text: Look up each file name through a content search instead
options.says: Ruled out because "Grep finds lines inside files, and Glob finds the files themselves", so a content search is the wrong tool for finding files.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, a developer-productivity agent. The agent explores unfamiliar codebases with the built-in tools. Asked to investigate how authentication works, it reads hundreds of files, and its answers get worse as the run goes on. What fixes it?

options.text: Read the whole repository once and write a summary of it
options.says: Ruled out because reading everything is the failure itself: "The infinite exploration. You ask Claude to 'investigate' something without scoping it. Claude reads hundreds of files, filling the context."

options.text: Raise the turn limit and let the agent finish its reading
options.says: Ruled out because more turns make the run longer and not better: "Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills."

options.text: Search for entry points, then follow imports a hop at a time
options.says: The cause is the context filling with files that do not matter, and the remedy is to scope the reading.

options.text: List every file name in the repository, then open each of them
options.says: Ruled out because opening every file in turn is the same unscoped reading: "Claude reads hundreds of files, filling the context."
